correctness.rationale: For both groups, the n-1 degree-two representations have rotation matrix diag(zeta^k,zeta^-k); their kernels are precisely the rotation powers annihilated by k, of size gcd(2n,k), so the codegree is 2n/gcd(2n,k). Exact-order residues modulo 2n occur in inverse pairs, giving phi(d)/2 characters of each codegree d>2. The only difference is the abelianization: C2 x C2 for the dihedral group and for even-parameter dicyclic groups, but C4 for odd-parameter dicyclic groups. The packaged checker independently verifies the resulting tables and parity criterion over a broad finite range.

value.rationale: The pseudo-algebra literature is explicitly concerned with what structural information the invariant retains and with constructing collisions. Dihedral and dicyclic groups are a canonical same-order split/non-split pair, and the theorem gives a complete parity classification of when the invariant distinguishes them. It yields an infinite, naturally parametrized collision family and explains the mechanism: the nonlinear codegrees coincide identically, while only the abelianization sees parity.
